content:
iOS 27 continues Apple's consistent trend of giving users more control over customizing the design of the iPhone lock screen. This year brings several new customization options, wallpaper settings and other features.

Extend Wallpaper

iOS 27 brings brand new Apple Intelligence editing features to the Photos app, including a redesigned "Clean Up" tool, as well as a "Recompose" feature. Another new option is "Extend," which can intelligently expand your images, allowing you to adjust the aspect ratio, straighten horizontal lines, or simply add more space at the edges.

As shown above, the "Extend" feature also comes to the lock screen in iOS 27. If a photo doesn't match your iPhone's aspect ratio, or isn't cropped enough to serve as a wallpaper, iOS 27 will automatically suggest using the "Extend" feature to fix it.

The "Extend" feature uses AI to generate additional image content at the edges, giving you more flexibility when setting a photo as your iPhone wallpaper.

Generate Your Own Wallpaper

iOS 27 brings major improvements to Image Playground, Apple's AI image generation app. Changes to Image Playground also extend to your iPhone's lock screen. Now, you can generate wallpapers using Image Playground directly from the Settings or the lock screen wallpaper picker.

In the wallpaper picker, you'll see a new "Image Playground" option. This feature creates stylized versions of images from your Photos library, such as "Retro Illustration" and "Animation," among others.

You can also use natural language to describe what you want, creating a custom wallpaper from scratch.

Move the Clock

iOS 27 finally lets you shrink the clock on the iPhone lock screen. Although Apple has let you customize the clock size for years, iOS 27 takes it a step further. Now, you can move the lock screen clock to the top widget row.

This frees up more space on the lock screen, letting you see more of your wallpaper. Of course, the trade-off is that it becomes harder to glance at the time from a distance. However, for many people, the point of the lock screen has always been to showcase the wallpaper, and iOS 27 makes this even easier.

Swipe Away the Now Playing Widget

In iOS 27, you can now swipe away the Now Playing widget on the iPhone lock screen. Even if you dismiss the Now Playing widget, whatever you're listening to will continue to play.

This feature is very useful if you often accidentally tap the Now Playing widget on the lock screen.

Wrap Up

iOS 27 is now available for developers and public beta testers, and will officially launch later this year. What do you think of the new lock screen customization features in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments section below.
